Housing materials—Competition among the various construction materials is encouraged in Operation Breakthrough. Some competition is certainly healthy but the outcome should not be the complete dominance of housing systems by one material. This project should include research to develop a mix of construction materials utilizing the best features of each and producing a variety of high quality products.
The statement should include a discussion of prior attempts to utilize various building materials such as plastic and metal for housing construction and analyze the factors that contributed to their continued use or disuse. Such an analysis would insure that environmental or sociological factors which may have been detrimental to the acceptance of such materials could be avoided. Examples could include the "Lustron home" manufactured by the Lustron Corporation, the various service stations which until recently involved enameled steel exteriors, or the all-plastic house that was constructed by the Monsanto Company. There are probably numerous additional examples of efforts to construct or market individually or mass-produced homes fabricated from such materials which would be helpful in statement preparation.
Inasmuch as the report deals with the environmental aspects of housing, some mention should be made of the use of solid waste materials in housing construction. The Department of the Interior through its Bureau of Mires has made extensive studies of the utilization of mining and mineral wastes, from many diverse sources, for structural units applicable to housing. We believe that inasmuch as wastes of this type constitute the largest growing resource of the United States, a notation of such resources for the future cught to be made.
